text:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a 2h profiler on the kernel-routing change on canary (small pool of V100s). Seeing batch formation stalls when KV cache churn spikes, and a few soft OOMs. baseline p50 gen = 12ms, under churn p50=40ms p95=120ms. trace: https://redwood.internal/trace/abc123 :thinking_face:

cheng: ugh. can you paste the top traces? is this kv growth (long prefixes) or a kernel fallback thrash?

maria: attaching snip of the admission log and kernel selection lines:
```
[2026-03-18T14:10:03Z] admit: batch_id=326 token_sum=4680 tokens_per_req=[120,240,432,388] decision=admit kernel=fast_attn_v2 kv_delta=+1.9GB headroom=1.1GB
[2026-03-18T14:10:03Z] kernel-fallback: kernel=matmul reason=kv_memory_pressure fallback_cost=+23ms
[2026-03-18T14:10:10Z] oom-soft: attempt_id=7 evicted=small-entries shed=2 requests_delayed=1
```

maria: kernel chooser is toggling between fast_attn_v2 and matmul because of memory footprint increases. fast_attn uses extra KV offsets for prefetched tokens which is fine usually but when 2 large-token requests join a batch KV blows past our soft headroom.

aj: this reads like admission is too permissive for token-thin vs token-heavy requests. we should gate by token_budget_target per-batch. current target=2048 on these V100s? drop to 1024 or 800 for canary. also set kv_headroom_margin=0.12. simple change, big win.

lucas: we tried lowering token_budget before, but it increased RPC qps (more batches) and upped CPU. tradeoff is cost vs OOM. however OOMs are worse for SLAs. can we prefer_small_requests=true in queue policy so small/interactive queries don't get stuck behind big ones?

eva: another lever: early-shepherding for requests that touch >X prefix tokens. mark them as kv-heavy and place in isolated admission queue with stricter budget. avoids mixing.

maria: agree with aj + eva. plan: 1) canary token_budget_target=800 2) kv_headroom_margin=0.12 3) enable prefer_small_requests=true 4) shepherd threshold=prefix_tokens>=512. will run 30m and collect headroom metrics.

cheng: add two metric checks for me: (a) kernel-fallback-rate > 0.5% (b) admitted_batch_kv_growth_mean > 0.5GB per batch. if either fires, rollback.

aj: small config snippet for runtime agent — deploy this to the canary pool:
```yaml
admission:
  token_budget_target: 800
  prefer_small_requests: true
  shepherd:
    kv_threshold_tokens: 512
kv:
  headroom_margin: 0.12
  soft_eviction: true
```

maria: deploying now to 5 canary machines. will post results.

ops-bot: Canary deployment started by @maria (canary-pool-v100-5) — rollout id: r-20260318-11 :rocket:

maria: initial 10m: kernel-fallback-rate down from 1.8% -> 0.4%, p95 latency back to ~18ms, one soft eviction event logged but no task OOMs. will keep running for 30m. :thumbsup:

lucas: nice. if stable, let's promote to the larger pool but watch CPU delta. we may need to tune batching window to coalesce more tiny requests to avoid cost spike.

eva: noted — adding a load-test for high small-request qps.

maria: leaving this thread with action items: run 4h extended canary, add cheng's alerts, metric dashboards for admitted KV growth, and follow-up meeting if rollback needed. thanks all.
